overdose_effects: Severe hypotension, stupor
kidney_liver_warning: Dose adjustment required in kidney impairment
how_it_works_in_body: Relaxes blood vessels, lowering blood pressure and reducing the heart's workload.
quick_summary: Effective blood pressure medication that also protects the heart and kidneys.
who_should_take: Patients with high blood pressure or heart failure.
who_should_not_take: Pregnant women or those with a history of angioedema.
alcohol_warning: May increase the blood pressure-lowering effect, causing dizziness.

mechanism_of_action: Cardioselective beta-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist
overdose_effects: Severe bradycardia, hypotension, heart failure
kidney_liver_warning: Use with caution in severe liver impairment
how_it_works_in_body: Slows the heart rate and reduces the force of heart muscle contraction.
quick_summary: Heart medication used to treat high blood pressure, chest pain, and heart failure.
who_should_take: Patients with cardiovascular conditions requiring heart rate control.
who_should_not_take: People with very slow heart rate or severe heart block.
food_interactions: Take with or immediately after meals

mechanism_of_action: Increases insulin sensitivity in muscle and adipose tissue
overdose_effects: Hypoglycemia (if taken with other anti-diabetics)
contraindications: Heart failure (NYHA Class III or IV)
how_it_works_in_body: Helps the body use insulin more effectively to lower blood sugar.
quick_summary: Improves insulin sensitivity to help control blood sugar in Type 2 Diabetes.
who_should_take: Patients with Type 2 Diabetes needing better glycemic control.
who_should_not_take: Individuals with severe heart failure or active bladder cancer.
alcohol_warning: May increase the risk of hypoglycemia.

mechanism_of_action: Stimulates insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells
overdose_effects: Severe hypoglycemia, coma, seizures
kidney_liver_warning: Avoid in severe kidney or liver impairment
how_it_works_in_body: Forces the pancreas to release more insulin to lower blood sugar levels.
quick_summary: Oral medication that stimulates the pancreas to produce more insulin.
who_should_take: Patients with Type 2 Diabetes whose pancreas still produces some insulin.
who_should_not_take: Patients with Type 1 Diabetes or severe kidney/liver disease.
food_interactions: Take with meals to prevent low blood sugar
alcohol_warning: Can cause severe hypoglycemia and a disulfiram-like reaction.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 30S ribosomal subunit
overdose_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea
kidney_liver_warning: Use with caution in liver impairment
how_it_works_in_body: Stops the growth and spread of bacteria.
quick_summary: Broad-spectrum antibiotic used for various bacterial infections and acne.
who_should_take: Patients with susceptible bacterial infections or severe acne.
food_interactions: Avoid dairy products, antacids, and iron supplements within 2 hours of taking
alcohol_warning: May decrease the effectiveness of the antibiotic.

mechanism_of_action: Synthetic version of the hormone thyroxine (T4) normally produced by thyroid gland.
dosage_common: 25mcg to 200mcg once daily, on empty stomach 30-60 mins before breakfast
overdose_effects: Thyroid storm, rapid heart rate, confusion.
pregnancy_safety: Category A - Safe and essential in pregnancy.
how_it_works_in_body: Replaces the missing thyroid hormone to regulate energy and metabolism.
quick_summary: Essential hormone replacement for patients with underactive thyroid.
who_should_not_take: Patients with untreated adrenal gland problems.
food_interactions: Fiber, walnuts, and soybean flour may decrease absorption.
alcohol_warning: Alcohol does not directly interact but can worsen fatigue.

mechanism_of_action: Relaxes the muscles in the airways and increases air flow to the lungs.
dosage_common: 1-2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for rescue
overdose_effects: Seizures, chest pain, nausea, extremely fast heartbeat.
pregnancy_safety: Category C - Use if benefit outweighs risk.
how_it_works_in_body: Quickly opens up the lung passages during an asthma attack.
quick_summary: Standard rescue inhaler for immediate relief from asthma symptoms.
who_should_take: Patients during acute asthma or COPD flare-ups.
who_should_not_take: Patients with certain heart rhythm disorders without consultation.
alcohol_warning: Avoid alcohol as it can trigger asthma symptoms in some people.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits cyclooxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2) to reduce pain and inflammation locally.
dosage_common: Apply a thin layer to the affected area 3-4 times daily
overdose_effects: Skin rash, stomach upset (if ingested).
pregnancy_safety: Category C/D - Avoid in late pregnancy.
kidney_liver_warning: Safe topically, but avoid large areas if severe impairment exists.
how_it_works_in_body: Penetrates the skin to reduce inflammation directly at the site of pain.
quick_summary: Widely used topical gel for immediate relief from muscle and joint pain.
who_should_take: People with localized pain, sprains, or arthritic discomfort.
who_should_not_take: People with broken skin or severe aspirin allergy.
alcohol_warning: No significant interaction with topical application.

mechanism_of_action: Helps the body absorb calcium and phosphorus, essential for building and maintaining strong bones.
dosage_common: 60,000 IU once weekly for 8-12 weeks, or as directed by a physician.
overdose_effects: Weakness, bone pain, metallic taste, excessive thirst.
pregnancy_safety: Generally safe when used in prescribed amounts.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with caution in kidney disease; monitor calcium levels.
how_it_works_in_body: Converted in the liver and kidneys to its active form, calcitriol, which assists in intestinal calcium absorption.
onset_of_action: Delayed; effects on calcium levels seen over several days.
duration_of_effect: Up to several weeks due to fat-soluble nature.
quick_summary: High-dose Vitamin D supplement used for correction of deficiency and bone health.
who_should_take: Individuals with diagnosed Vitamin D deficiency or bone density issues.
who_should_not_take: Those with hypercalcemia or known hypersensitivity to Vitamin D.
food_interactions: Better absorbed when taken with a fatty meal.
alcohol_warning: No significant interaction, but alcohol can interfere with calcium absorption.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits the fungal enzyme cytochrome P450 14α-demethylase, which is critical for fungal cell membrane synthesis.
dosage_common: 100-200mg once or twice daily depending on infection severity.
overdose_effects: Severe nausea, abdominal pain, visual disturbances.
contraindications: Concurrent use of certain statins or ergot alkaloids
pregnancy_safety: Not recommended during pregnancy unless strictly necessary.
kidney_liver_warning: Caution in liver disease; regular monitoring of liver function tests (LFTs) required.
how_it_works_in_body: Broad-spectrum antifungal that prevents fungal growth by damaging cell membranes.
onset_of_action: Peak concentrations usually reached within 2-5 hours.
duration_of_effect: Long half-life; remains in the body for several days.
quick_summary: Efficient antifungal medication for internal and external fungal infections.
who_should_take: Patients with confirmed fungal infections under medical supervision.
who_should_not_take: Individuals with heart failure or severe liver impairment.
food_interactions: Absorption is increased with acidic food/drinks like cola or juice.
alcohol_warning: Avoid; increases the risk of liver damage.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits the Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme, preventing the production of a substance that narrows blood vessels.
overdose_effects: Severe hypotension, electrolyte disturbances, renal failure.
pregnancy_safety: Unsafe; can cause serious injury or death to the developing fetus.
kidney_liver_warning: Caution in renal impairment; monitoring of potassium and creatinine is essential.
how_it_works_in_body: Relaxes blood vessels and reduces workload on the heart by blocking angiotensin II formation.
quick_summary: Leading medication for blood pressure control and cardiovascular protection.
who_should_take: Adults with hypertension or recovered heart attack patients.
who_should_not_take: Pregnant women or those with a history of serious allergic reactions to ACE inhibitors.
food_interactions: Food does not significantly affect absorption.
alcohol_warning: Can significantly increase the blood-pressure-lowering effect leading to dizziness.

mechanism_of_action: Kills bacteria by preventing them from forming their own protective covering (cell wall).
overdose_effects: Could cause neurological irritation including seizures.
pregnancy_safety: Considered safe, but only use if clearly needed.
kidney_liver_warning: Dosage adjustment might be needed in severe kidney disease.
how_it_works_in_body: Broad-spectrum activity against both Gram-positive and some Gram-negative bacteria.
quick_summary: Potent antibiotic for community-acquired bacterial infections.
who_should_take: Individuals with bacterial infections confirmed by a doctor.
who_should_not_take: Those with history of severe penicillin allergy.
food_interactions: Should be taken after food for better absorption and to reduce stomach upset.
alcohol_warning: No major interaction, but best to avoid during infections.

mechanism_of_action: Blocks L-type and N-type calcium channels, dilating blood vessels and reducing nerve-mediated constriction.
overdose_effects: Severe dizziness, fainting, rapid or slow heartbeat.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with caution in patients with liver or kidney dysfunction.
how_it_works_in_body: Unique L/N-type channel blocking prevents reflex tachycardia (racing heart) often seen with other CCBs.
quick_summary: Modern antihypertensive that is gentler on the heart rate compared to older alternatives.
who_should_take: Patients with hypertension, especially those who experience safe swelling with other drugs.
who_should_not_take: Individuals with very low blood pressure or serious heart valve issues.
alcohol_warning: Increases risk of low blood pressure and fainting.

mechanism_of_action: Prevents platelets (blood cells) from sticking together and forming dangerous blood clots.
overdose_effects: Excessive bleeding, vomiting blood, black stools.
pregnancy_safety: Generally discouraged unless high risk; consult doctor.
kidney_liver_warning: No major adjustment usually needed, but monitor carefully in liver disease.
how_it_works_in_body: Irreversibly binds to platelet receptors for the duration of the platelet's life (7-10 days).
onset_of_action: Loading dose takes 2 hours; regular 75mg takes 3-7 days for full effect.
duration_of_effect: Up to 5 days after stopping the drug.
quick_summary: Critical medication for preventing blood clots in heart disease patients.
who_should_take: Individuals with heart stents or history of stroke/heart attack.
who_should_not_take: People with current active bleeding or upcoming major surgery.
food_interactions: Can be taken with or without food.
alcohol_warning: Increases the risk of stomach bleeding.

mechanism_of_action: Replaces enzymes that are normally produced by the pancreas to help digest fats, proteins, and sugars.
dosage_common: Varies by meal size; usually 25,000-50,000 units per full meal.
overdose_effects: High uric acid in blood/urine, severe constipation.
contraindications: Known allergy to pork protein (enzymes are porcine-derived)
pregnancy_safety: Generally considered safe as it acts locally in the gut.
kidney_liver_warning: No major warnings; use with medical guidance.
how_it_works_in_body: Enteric-coated microspheres release amylase, protease, and lipase in the small intestine to break down food.
duration_of_effect: Limited to the transit time of food.
quick_summary: Essential replacement therapy for patients who cannot digest food naturally.
who_should_take: Patients with pancreatic insufficiency or chronic digestive issues.
who_should_not_take: Those with pork allergies or acute pancreatic flare-ups.
food_interactions: MUST be taken with every meal and snack to be effective.
alcohol_warning: No direct interaction, but alcohol significantly worsens pancreatic disease.

mechanism_of_action: Reduces cholesterol production in the liver and clears 'bad' cholesterol (LDL) from the blood.
dosage_common: 5mg to 40mg once daily, usually at night.
overdose_effects: Increased muscle pain symptoms, nausea.
pregnancy_safety: UNSAFE; causes significant risk of birth defects.
kidney_liver_warning: Monitor LFTs regularly; check kidney function at high doses.
how_it_works_in_body: Potent statin that significantly lowers LDL and raises 'good' HDL cholesterol.
duration_of_effect: Longer-acting statin; blood levels remain significant for 24 hours.
quick_summary: Gold-standard medication for lowering cholesterol and preventing heart disease.
who_should_take: Individuals with high LDL levels or cardiovascular risk factors.
who_should_not_take: Pregnant women or those with active liver inflammation.
food_interactions: Can be taken with or without food.
alcohol_warning: Limit; increases risk of liver issues and muscle pain.

mechanism_of_action: Rabeprazole reduces stomach acid; Domperidone increases gut movement to prevent reflux.
dosage_common: One capsule daily, 30 minutes before breakfast.
overdose_effects: Agitation, confusion, drowsiness, seizures (rare).
pregnancy_safety: Use only if essential; consult doctor.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with caution in moderate to severe liver disease.
how_it_works_in_body: Provides 24-hour acid suppression and improves gastric emptying.
onset_of_action: Acid relief in 1 hour; motion effect in 30-60 mins.
quick_summary: Effective combination for treating severe acidity accompanied by nausea.
who_should_take: Patients with acid reflux who also experience bloating or nausea.
who_should_not_take: Patients with existing heart rhythm conditions.
food_interactions: MUST be taken on an empty stomach for maximum effect.
alcohol_warning: Avoid; increases acid secretion and reduces drug effectiveness.

drug_name: A to Z Multivitamin with Minerals and Pine Bark Extract Tablet
mechanism_of_action: Provides essential micronutrients that act as co-enzymes and co-factors for various metabolic processes while antioxidants like Pine Bark Extract neutralize free radicals to prevent oxidative stress.
uses: Supportive therapy during recovery from surgery or chronic illness
dosage_common: One tablet daily, preferably after a meal to maximize absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.
side_effects_serious: Severe allergic reactions (hives, swelling of face/tongue)
overdose_effects: Overdose can lead to toxicity, particularly from fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E), resulting in severe nausea, blurred vision, headache, and potential liver or kidney stress.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to any of the ingredients
drug_interactions: Warfarin (Vitamin E may enhance anticoagulant effect)
pregnancy_safety: Category A/B: Generally considered safe and often prescribed during pregnancy, but dosage should be strictly monitored by a healthcare professional.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with caution in patients with chronic kidney disease or liver dysfunction as they may have difficulty excreting excess minerals.
how_it_works_in_body: The B-vitamins aid in energy metabolism, Vitamin C and E along with Pine Bark Extract act as antioxidants to protect cellular integrity, and minerals like Zinc and Selenium support enzyme functions and immune response.
onset_of_action: 1 to 2 weeks for noticeable improvement in energy levels and general well-being.
india_regulatory_status: FSSAI / CDSCO Approved as a Nutraceutical/Drug supplement
quick_summary: A TO Z TAB is a comprehensive health supplement containing vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants designed to bridge nutritional gaps and support the body's immune system.
who_should_take: Individuals with a poor diet, those recovering from illness, people with high physical activity levels, or those feeling chronically fatigued.
who_should_not_take: Those with known allergies to multivitamin components or individuals suffering from copper or iron storage disorders.
food_interactions: Avoid taking with tea or coffee as tannins and caffeine can inhibit the absorption of vitamins and minerals.
alcohol_warning: Alcohol does not directly interact with the tablet, but chronic consumption can deplete the body's vitamin stores, making the supplement less effective.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time for your next dose, skip it and continue your regular schedule. Do not double the dose.

mechanism_of_action: Bactericidal action resulting from inhibition of cell-wall synthesis. It binds to one or more of the penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) which in turn inhibits the final transpeptidation step of peptidoglycan synthesis in bacterial cell walls.
uses: Acute Bronchitis and Chronic Bronchitis Exacerbations
dosage_common: Adults: 200 mg to 400 mg daily, taken either as a single dose or in two divided doses every 12 hours.
overdose_effects: Symptoms may include nausea, vomiting, and epigastric distress. In case of severe overdose, gastric lavage may be indicated; there is a risk of seizures in patients with renal impairment.
contraindications: History of severe immediate hypersensitivity to Penicillin
pregnancy_safety: Category B: Studies in animals have failed to demonstrate a risk to the fetus, but there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Use only if clearly needed.
kidney_liver_warning: Dose adjustment is required for patients with significant renal impairment (creatinine clearance < 20 mL/min). Use with caution in patients with pre-existing liver disease.
how_it_works_in_body: Once ingested, cefixime reaches peak plasma levels and interferes with the enzymes responsible for making the bacterial cell wall. This weakens the cell wall, causing the bacteria to rupture and die, effectively clearing the infection.
quick_summary: ABIXIM-200 is an oral cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections by stopping the growth of bacteria.
who_should_take: Individuals with bacterial infections of the respiratory tract, urinary tract, or ear, as diagnosed and prescribed by a healthcare professional.
who_should_not_take: Individuals with a known allergy to cephalosporins or penicillins, and those with a history of severe gastrointestinal disease like colitis.
food_interactions: Can be taken with or without food
Taking with food may help reduce gastrointestinal upset
alcohol_warning: While no direct interaction is established, alcohol should be avoided as it can increase the risk of side effects like dizziness and nausea.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose. Do not take extra medicine to make up the missed dose.

drug_class: Analgesic, Antipyretic, and Proteolytic Enzyme Combination
mechanism_of_action: Aceclofenac inhibits the cyclooxygenase (COX) enzyme, reducing prostaglandin synthesis; Paracetamol acts on the central nervous system to increase pain threshold and reduce fever; Serratiopeptidase is a proteolytic enzyme that breaks down abnormal proteins at the site of inflammation to promote tissue repair and reduce edema.
dosage_common: One tablet twice daily after meals, or as prescribed by a physician.
overdose_effects: Common symptoms include severe vomiting, gastric irritation, hepatic tenderness, and in severe cases, liver necrosis or acute renal failure due to high paracetamol levels.
contraindications: Active peptic ulcer or GI bleeding
pregnancy_safety: Category C/D: Generally not recommended, especially in the third trimester as it may cause premature closure of the ductus arteriosus in the fetus.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with extreme caution in patients with hepatic or renal impairment; dose adjustment may be required. Avoid use in severe failure.
how_it_works_in_body: The combination provides a multi-modal approach: it blocks pain signals at the site of injury (Aceclofenac), raises the overall pain threshold via the brain (Paracetamol), and physically breaks down inflammatory debris to reduce swelling (Serratiopeptidase).
quick_summary: A combination medication used to relieve pain, inflammation, and swelling in various conditions involving bones, joints, and soft tissues.
who_should_take: Individuals suffering from acute inflammatory pain, post-surgical inflammation, or chronic joint disorders under medical supervision.
who_should_not_take: Individuals with a history of stomach ulcers, bleeding disorders, severe liver/kidney disease, or those allergic to aspirin and other NSAIDs.
food_interactions: Take with food or milk to minimize gastric irritation.
alcohol_warning: Strictly avoid alcohol as it significantly increases the risk of gastric bleeding and liver toxicity when combined with Paracetamol and Aceclofenac.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double the dose to catch up.

drug_class: NSAID (Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drug) and Analgesic Combination
mechanism_of_action: Aceclofenac inhibits the enzyme cyclooxygenase (COX), which is involved in the synthesis of prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol acts primarily on the central nervous system to increase the pain threshold and regulate body temperature via the hypothalamus.
dosage_common: Adults: Usually one tablet twice daily (morning and evening) taken after food to prevent stomach upset.
overdose_effects: Nausea, vomiting, and epigastric pain are common. High doses of Paracetamol can lead to fatal hepatic necrosis and renal tubular necrosis.
contraindications: History of asthma attacks induced by Aspirin or NSAIDs
pregnancy_safety: Category D - Not recommended, especially during the third trimester, as it may cause premature closure of the ductus arteriosus in the fetus and delay labor.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with caution in patients with mild to moderate renal or hepatic impairment. Contraindicated in severe cases. Long-term use can lead to nephrotoxicity.
how_it_works_in_body: After oral administration, the drugs are rapidly absorbed. Aceclofenac targets peripheral inflammation sites to reduce swelling and pain, while Paracetamol provides a systemic analgesic and antipyretic effect, effectively managing the perception of pain and reducing fever.
quick_summary: Aceclo Plus is a widely used combination medicine in India for managing moderate to severe pain and inflammation associated with arthritis and injuries.
who_should_take: Adults experiencing acute pain, inflammatory joint conditions, or musculoskeletal pain as prescribed by a physician.
who_should_not_take: Individuals with a history of stomach ulcers, severe heart/kidney/liver disease, pregnant women in their third trimester, and those allergic to NSAIDs.
food_interactions: Take with food or milk to reduce gastric irritation.
Avoid chronic use with high-protein diets which may affect absorption slightly.
alcohol_warning: Avoid alcohol as it significantly increases the risk of stomach bleeding and enhances the hepatotoxic effects of Paracetamol.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it. Do not double the dose to catch up.

mechanism_of_action: Acenocoumarol inhibits the enzyme vitamin K epoxide reductase, which results in the depletion of the reduced form of vitamin K (vitamin KH2). This depletion prevents the gamma-carboxylation of glutamic acid residues on the vitamin K-dependent clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X, as well as anticoagulant proteins C and S, rendering them inactive.
uses: Prevention and treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
Prophylaxis of thromboembolism in atrial fibrillation
Management of thromboembolic risk in patients with prosthetic heart valves
Treatment of myocardial infarction to reduce the risk of systemic embolism
dosage_common: Dosage is highly individualized and must be adjusted based on regular International Normalized Ratio (INR) blood tests. A typical maintenance dose ranges from 1mg to 8mg daily, taken at the same time each day.
overdose_effects: The primary symptom of overdose is excessive bleeding from various sites. Symptoms include ecchymosis, hematuria, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and uterine bleeding. Treatment usually involves administration of Vitamin K1 (Phytonadione) and potentially fresh frozen plasma or prothrombin complex concentrate.
contraindications: Recent surgery of the eye, brain, or spinal cord
pregnancy_safety: Category X: Acenocoumarol is contraindicated in pregnancy as it crosses the placental barrier and can cause fetal warfarin syndrome, including nasal hypoplasia and skeletal abnormalities, as well as fatal fetal hemorrhage.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with extreme caution. Liver impairment reduces the synthesis of clotting factors and metabolism of the drug. Kidney impairment increases the risk of over-anticoagulation and bleeding complications.
how_it_works_in_body: After oral administration, it is rapidly absorbed. It acts in the liver to block the recycling of Vitamin K. Since the body relies on Vitamin K to produce functional clotting factors, the blood's ability to form clots is significantly delayed. It does not dissolve existing clots but prevents them from enlarging or new ones from forming.
onset_of_action: 24 to 48 hours (Peak effect reached in 72 to 96 hours)
duration_of_effect: 48 to 72 hours after the last dose
quick_summary: Acitrom 4mg is a potent anticoagulant used to prevent unwanted blood clots that can lead to stroke, heart attack, or pulmonary embolism. It requires strict medical supervision and regular INR monitoring.
who_should_take: Patients diagnosed with conditions putting them at high risk for thromboembolic events, such as those with artificial heart valves or chronic atrial fibrillation.
who_should_not_take: Pregnant women, individuals with a high risk of falling, people with active bleeding disorders, or those unable to comply with regular blood testing schedules.
food_interactions: Foods high in Vitamin K (Spinach, Kale, Broccoli, Cabbage) - can decrease effectiveness
Cranberry juice - may increase the effect/bleeding risk
alcohol_warning: Avoid or strictly limit alcohol. Binge drinking can increase the risk of bleeding, while chronic heavy drinking may decrease the drug's effectiveness.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as possible on the same day. If it is almost time for the next day's dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double the dose. Inform your doctor about the missed dose during your next INR check.

mechanism_of_action: Acyclovir is a synthetic purine nucleoside analogue. It is converted to acyclovir monophosphate by viral thymidine kinase, then further to triphosphate by cellular enzymes. Acyclovir triphosphate competitively inhibits viral DNA polymerase and incorporates into viral DNA, resulting in DNA chain termination.
uses: Treatment of Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV-1, HSV-2) infections
dosage_common: Usually 200 mg taken five times daily at 4-hour intervals (skipping the night dose) for 5 to 10 days. The tablet should be dissolved in a glass of water before consumption.
overdose_effects: Overdosage may lead to elevations in serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, and subsequent renal failure. Neurological effects such as confusion, hallucinations, and agitation may also occur.
pregnancy_safety: Category B: Use only if clearly needed. Animal studies show no fetal risk, but adequate human studies are limited.
kidney_liver_warning: Dose adjustment is mandatory in patients with renal impairment to prevent neurotoxicity and renal crystal formation. Use with caution in patients with hepatic disease.
how_it_works_in_body: After oral administration, acyclovir is partially absorbed from the gut. It selectively enters cells infected with the herpes virus. Once inside, it undergoes phosphorylation into its active form, which blocks the virus's ability to replicate its genetic material (DNA), thereby stopping the spread of the infection.
duration_of_effect: 4 to 8 hours (Half-life is approximately 2.5 to 3.3 hours in adults with normal renal function)
quick_summary: ACIVIR 200MG DT is a widely used antiviral medication in India primarily for treating herpes and chickenpox by stopping viral replication.
who_should_take: Patients suffering from initial or recurrent mucosal or cutaneous herpes simplex infections or shingles as diagnosed by a healthcare professional.
who_should_not_take: Those with known allergies to acyclovir or valacyclovir, and patients with severely impaired kidney function unless the dose is specifically adjusted.
food_interactions: Can be taken with or without food; no major food interactions noted.
alcohol_warning: Avoid alcohol as it may increase dizziness and dehydration, potentially worsening side effects or putting additional strain on the kidneys.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not take two doses at once.

mechanism_of_action: Acyclovir is converted to acyclovir triphosphate by viral and cellular enzymes. This triphosphate acts as a false substrate for viral DNA polymerase, competing with natural dGTP and leading to viral DNA chain termination.
uses: Treatment of Herpes Simplex virus infections (Genital Herpes and Cold Sores)
Prevention of recurrent Herpes Simplex infections in immunocompromised patients
dosage_common: Usually 400mg three to five times daily for 5-10 days depending on the severity and type of infection. The dispersible tablet should be dissolved in a glass of water before administration.
overdose_effects: Overdose may lead to elevated serum creatinine, renal failure, agitation, coma, and seizures. Hemodialysis may be required to remove the drug from the blood.
pregnancy_safety: Category B: Generally considered safe. Studies in animals have not shown fetal risk, but it should be used in pregnancy only if clearly needed and prescribed by a doctor.
kidney_liver_warning: Dose adjustment is mandatory in patients with renal impairment to prevent drug accumulation and neurotoxicity. Use with caution in patients with underlying liver disease.
how_it_works_in_body: Once ingested, the drug is selectively taken up by virus-infected cells. Viral thymidine kinase converts it into acyclovir monophosphate, which is further phosphorylated to the active triphosphate form. This active form halts the replication of viral DNA, stopping the spread of the virus in the body.
duration_of_effect: 4 to 6 hours (Half-life is approximately 2.5 to 3.3 hours in adults with normal renal function)
india_regulatory_status: CDSCO Approved; Schedule H Prescription Drug
quick_summary: Acivir 400mg DT is a potent antiviral medication used to manage and treat infections caused by the herpes virus, including shingles, chickenpox, and genital herpes.
who_should_take: Individuals diagnosed with viral infections such as herpes simplex or herpes zoster, particularly those who prefer or require a dispersible tablet format.
who_should_not_take: Individuals with a known allergy to Acyclovir or Valacyclovir and patients with severe, unmonitored kidney disease.
food_interactions: Can be taken with or without food
High fluid intake is recommended to maintain hydration and renal flow
alcohol_warning: Alcohol should be avoided as it can worsen side effects like dizziness and may increase the risk of dehydration, impacting kidney function during treatment.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not double the dose to catch up.

mechanism_of_action: It works by inhibiting viral DNA synthesis. It is converted by viral thymidine kinase into acyclovir monophosphate, which is then further converted into acyclovir triphosphate. This triphosphate competes with deoxyguanosine triphosphate for viral DNA polymerase and becomes incorporated into viral DNA, causing DNA chain termination.
dosage_common: For Shingles: 800mg five times daily (every 4 hours while awake) for 7 to 10 days. For Chickenpox: 800mg four times daily for 5 days. Must be dissolved in water before consumption.
overdose_effects: High doses may lead to elevated serum creatinine, renal failure, agitation, coma, and seizures. Hemodialysis may be required to remove the drug from the blood.
contraindications: Known allergy to any component of the dispersible tablet
drug_interactions: Nephrotoxic agents like Aminoglycosides or NSAIDs
pregnancy_safety: Category B: Studies in animals have not shown a risk to the fetus, but there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Use only if clearly needed.
kidney_liver_warning: Dose adjustment is mandatory in patients with renal impairment. Use with caution in patients with pre-existing liver disease, though primary clearance is renal.
how_it_works_in_body: Once ingested and absorbed, it selectively targets cells infected with the Herpes virus. The viral enzyme thymidine kinase activates the drug, which then prevents the virus from replicating its genetic material, thereby stopping the spread of the infection and allowing the immune system to manage the virus.
duration_of_effect: The half-life is approximately 2.5 to 3.3 hours in adults with normal renal function.
india_regulatory_status: CDSCO Approved; Schedule H Prescription Drug
quick_summary: Acivir 800mg DT is a high-strength antiviral dispersible tablet used primarily to treat severe viral infections like shingles and chickenpox by stopping viral replication.
who_should_take: Adults and children (as per weight-based dosing) suffering from Herpes Zoster or Varicella infections within 24-48 hours of rash onset.
who_should_not_take: Dehydrated patients, those with significant kidney dysfunction without dose adjustment, or those with known hypersensitivity to acyclovir.
food_interactions: High fluid intake is recommended to prevent crystals from forming in the kidneys
alcohol_warning: While there is no direct interaction, alcohol can cause dehydration and dizziness, which may worsen the side effects of the medication.
missed_dose: Take it as soon as you remember. If it is nearly time for your next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double the dose to catch up.

mechanism_of_action: Acyclovir is converted by viral thymidine kinase into acyclovir monophosphate, which is then converted by host cell kinases into acyclovir triphosphate. This metabolite competes with deoxyguanosine triphosphate as a substrate for viral DNA polymerase and is incorporated into viral DNA, causing premature DNA chain termination.
dosage_common: Apply to the affected area 5 times daily (approximately every 4 hours while awake) for 4 to 10 days.
overdose_effects: Topical overdose is unlikely due to low systemic absorption. If accidentally ingested, symptoms may include gastrointestinal upset or neurological effects if large quantities are consumed.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to any excipients in the cream base
drug_interactions: Probenecid (may increase systemic levels if significant absorption occurs)
Other topical medications applied to the same site
pregnancy_safety: Category B: Studies in animals have not shown a risk to the fetus, but there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Use only if clearly needed.
kidney_liver_warning: Systemic absorption through topical application is minimal, making it generally safe for patients with kidney or liver impairment; however, caution is advised in severe renal failure if extensive areas are treated.
how_it_works_in_body: When applied topically, acyclovir penetrates the skin layers to reach the site of viral replication. It selectively targets cells infected with the Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV), where it halts the production of viral DNA, preventing the virus from multiplying and spreading to healthy cells.
onset_of_action: Symptomatic relief usually begins within 24 to 48 hours of starting treatment.
duration_of_effect: The medication remains active at the site of application for several hours; regular dosing is required to maintain therapeutic levels.
quick_summary: Acivir Cream is a topical antiviral medication used to treat cold sores and skin infections caused by the Herpes Simplex Virus.
who_should_take: Individuals suffering from recurrent cold sores (Herpes Labialis) or initial/recurrent genital herpes lesions.
who_should_not_take: Patients with known hypersensitivity to acyclovir or valacyclovir; not for use on mucous membranes like the inside of the mouth, eyes, or vagina.
alcohol_warning: No known interactions with alcohol for the topical cream formulation.
missed_dose: Apply the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double the application.

mechanism_of_action: Racecadotril acts as a prodrug that is hydrolyzed to thiorphan, which inhibits enkephalinase. This prevents the degradation of endogenous enkephalins, reducing intestinal hypersecretion of water and electrolytes without affecting gut motility.
uses: Symptomatic relief of sudden onset diarrhea
dosage_common: 100 mg orally three times a day, preferably before meals, continued until two normal stools are recorded, not exceeding 7 days of treatment.
overdose_effects: No specific symptoms of overdose have been reported, but it may lead to an intensification of common side effects like nausea or abdominal pain.
drug_interactions: No significant drug-drug interactions have been reported in humans
ACE Inhibitors (may increase risk of angioedema)
pregnancy_safety: Category B. Limited data available; use during pregnancy is not recommended unless the potential benefit justifies the risk.
kidney_liver_warning: Not recommended for patients with severe kidney or liver disease as clinical data is insufficient for these populations.
how_it_works_in_body: It is rapidly absorbed and converted into its active metabolite, thiorphan. Thiorphan binds to the active site of enkephalinase, preventing it from breaking down enkephalins in the small intestine. This results in decreased levels of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP), thereby reducing the secretion of water and electrolytes into the gut lumen.
quick_summary: AD 100MG (Racecadotril) is an anti-secretory drug used to treat acute diarrhea by reducing excessive fluid secretion in the intestines without causing constipation.
who_should_take: Adults experiencing acute, non-infectious diarrhea where fluid loss is a concern.
who_should_not_take: Children (unless specifically prescribed pediatric formulations), pregnant or breastfeeding women, and those with blood or pus in their stools (dysentery).
food_interactions: None significant; can be taken with or without food, though before meals is often preferred.
alcohol_warning: No direct interaction, but alcohol should be avoided during diarrhea as it can worsen dehydration and gastrointestinal irritation.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with the regular schedule. Do not double the dose.

mechanism_of_action: Acts directly on both alpha and beta-adrenergic receptors of the sympathetic nervous system to produce rapid systemic effects including vasoconstriction and bronchodilation.
dosage_common: Anaphylaxis: 0.3mg to 0.5mg (1:1000) IM in the mid-outer thigh. Cardiac Arrest: 1mg (1:10,000) IV/IO every 3 to 5 minutes.
overdose_effects: Extreme elevation in blood pressure which may lead to cerebrovascular hemorrhage, cardiac arrhythmias, and acute pulmonary edema due to peripheral vasoconstriction.
contraindications: Use with local anesthetics in distal appendages (fingers, toes, nose)
pregnancy_safety: Category C: Potential benefits may warrant use in pregnant women despite potential risks in life-threatening emergencies.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with caution; adrenaline can cause renal artery constriction and transiently decrease renal blood flow.
how_it_works_in_body: By stimulating Alpha-1 receptors, it causes vasoconstriction to increase blood pressure. Stimulating Beta-1 receptors increases heart rate and contractility. Stimulating Beta-2 receptors leads to bronchodilation and decreased release of inflammatory mediators from mast cells.
onset_of_action: IV: Immediate; IM: 5-10 minutes; Subcutaneous: 10-15 minutes
quick_summary: Adrenaline is a life-saving injection used primarily for emergency treatment of severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) and for restoring heart function during cardiac arrest.
who_should_take: Patients experiencing life-threatening allergic reactions, severe asthma attacks not responding to other treatments, or cardiac arrest.
who_should_not_take: Individuals with hypersensitivity (in non-emergency cases); use with extreme caution in patients with hyperthyroidism, hypertension, or heart disease.
food_interactions: Not applicable as it is administered parenterally in emergencies.
alcohol_warning: Avoid alcohol as it can exacerbate the cardiovascular side effects like increased heart rate and blood pressure fluctuations.
missed_dose: Not applicable as this is an emergency medication administered by healthcare professionals or via auto-injector when needed.

mechanism_of_action: Aldactone (Spironolactone) is a competitive antagonist of aldosterone. It binds to the mineralocorticoid receptors in the distal renal tubules, which blocks the exchange of sodium for potassium, resulting in increased excretion of sodium and water while retaining potassium.
uses: Edema associated with Congestive Heart Failure
Cirrhosis of the liver with ascites
dosage_common: Usually ranges from 25mg to 100mg daily, either in single or divided doses, based on the condition being treated.
overdose_effects: Overdose may lead to drowsiness, mental confusion, maculopapular or erythematous rash, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or diarrhea. Severe hyperkalemia may result in cardiac arrest.
pregnancy_safety: Category C: Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. It has anti-androgenic effects that may affect male fetus development.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with extreme caution in patients with hepatic dysfunction to avoid hepatic coma. In renal impairment, the risk of hyperkalemia is significantly increased; regular monitoring of serum potassium and creatinine is mandatory.
how_it_works_in_body: In the kidney, aldosterone normally causes the body to hold onto salt and water while losing potassium. By blocking aldosterone, Aldactone makes the kidneys eliminate more water and sodium through urine but keeps potassium in the bloodstream, helping to reduce fluid buildup and lower blood pressure.
onset_of_action: 24 to 48 hours for diuretic effect; 2 to 3 weeks for maximum antihypertensive effect.
duration_of_effect: 48 to 72 hours after the last dose.
quick_summary: Aldactone 25mg is a potassium-sparing diuretic used to treat high blood pressure, fluid retention (edema), and conditions involving excess aldosterone production.
who_should_take: Patients suffering from edema due to heart, liver, or kidney issues, or those with resistant hypertension requiring a diuretic that does not deplete potassium.
who_should_not_take: Individuals with high potassium levels, severe kidney failure, or those who cannot produce urine (anuria).
alcohol_warning: Alcohol may enhance the blood pressure lowering effect of Aldactone, increasing the risk of dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your normal schedule. Do not double the dose.

drug_class: Antihistamine and Alpha-1 Adrenergic Agonist Combination
mechanism_of_action: Cetirizine is a potent and selective peripheral H1-receptor antagonist that reduces allergic responses. Phenylephrine is a sympathomimetic amine that acts as a decongestant by stimulating alpha-adrenergic receptors, leading to vasoconstriction of nasal mucosa blood vessels.
dosage_common: Usually one tablet twice daily for adults and children over 12 years, or as directed by a physician.
overdose_effects: Symptoms may include extreme restlessness, severe drowsiness, palpitations, chest pain, and significantly elevated blood pressure.
contraindications: Patients taking MAO inhibitors within the last 14 days
pregnancy_safety: Category C: Use only if prescribed by a doctor. Phenylephrine should be avoided during the first trimester as it may affect fetal blood flow.
kidney_liver_warning: Dose reduction is necessary for patients with moderate to severe renal impairment. Use with caution in patients with hepatic dysfunction.
how_it_works_in_body: Cetirizine prevents histamine from binding to its receptors, stopping the allergic cascade. Simultaneously, Phenylephrine reduces the swelling of blood vessels in the nasal passages, allowing for easier breathing and drainage of mucus.
quick_summary: Alerid D is a combination medication primarily used to treat allergy symptoms accompanied by nasal congestion, combining an antihistamine with a decongestant.
who_should_take: Individuals experiencing allergic rhinitis along with blocked nose or sinus pressure.
who_should_not_take: Individuals with heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or those taking antidepressants belonging to the MAOI class.
alcohol_warning: Avoid consumption as it may significantly increase the sedative effect and impair motor skills.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double the dose.

mechanism_of_action: Amitriptyline works primarily by inhibiting the reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin at the nerve endings, which increases the concentration of these neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft, thereby enhancing mood and modulating pain signals.
dosage_common: Usually starts at 10mg to 25mg once daily at bedtime; dosage may be increased gradually based on clinical response and tolerability.
overdose_effects: Overdose can be fatal and includes symptoms such as severe cardiac arrhythmias, extreme hypotension, convulsions, hallucinations, and CNS depression leading to coma.
contraindications: Concurrent use of Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitors (MAOIs)
pregnancy_safety: Category C: Use only if potential benefits outweigh risks; can cause withdrawal symptoms in neonates if used in the third trimester.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with caution in patients with hepatic impairment due to reduced metabolism. Use with care in patients with severe renal impairment.
how_it_works_in_body: After oral administration, it is rapidly absorbed and metabolized in the liver to its active metabolite, nortriptyline. It acts on the central nervous system to increase levels of serotonin and norepinephrine while also exerting anticholinergic and sedative effects.
onset_of_action: 2 to 4 weeks for antidepressant effect; 1 week for chronic pain relief.
quick_summary: Amitone 10mg is a tricyclic antidepressant used for treating clinical depression, chronic nerve pain, and preventing migraine attacks.
who_should_take: Individuals diagnosed with depression or chronic neuropathic pain conditions under the supervision of a psychiatrist or neurologist.
who_should_not_take: Those with heart block, a history of recent heart attack, acute glaucoma, or those hypersensitive to tricyclic antidepressants.
alcohol_warning: Strictly avoid alcohol as it significantly increases drowsiness, dizziness, and central nervous system depression.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses at once.

mechanism_of_action: Amoxicillin works by inhibiting the synthesis of bacterial cell walls. Potassium Clavulanate is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that prevents bacteria from destroying amoxicillin, thereby extending its spectrum of activity against resistant strains.
dosage_common: Adults: Usually one tablet of 625 mg twice or thrice daily depending on the severity of the infection, taken for 5 to 10 days.
overdose_effects: Symptoms may include stomach pain, diarrhea, vomiting, skin rash, drowsiness, and hyperactivity. In some cases, interstitial nephritis leading to oliguric renal failure has been reported.
contraindications: History of cholestatic jaundice or liver dysfunction associated with Amoxyclav
pregnancy_safety: Category B; Generally considered safe if prescribed by a physician, but should only be used if clearly needed.
kidney_liver_warning: Dose adjustment is necessary for patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 ml/min). Use with caution in patients with hepatic dysfunction; monitoring of liver function is recommended.
how_it_works_in_body: After oral administration, both components are rapidly absorbed. Amoxicillin binds to penicillin-binding proteins inside the bacterial cell wall, causing cell lysis. Clavulanic acid binds to and inactivates beta-lactamase enzymes produced by bacteria that would otherwise deactivate the amoxicillin.
quick_summary: Amoxyclav 625 is a potent combination antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections, including those resistant to simple penicillin, by combining a cell-wall inhibitor with a protective enzyme inhibitor.
who_should_take: Patients diagnosed with bacterial infections of the lungs, ears, sinuses, urinary tract, or skin caused by organisms susceptible to this combination.
who_should_not_take: Individuals with a known allergy to penicillin or cephalosporin antibiotics, or those with a history of liver problems caused by this medication.
food_interactions: Take with food to minimize gastrointestinal intolerance and enhance absorption of Potassium Clavulanate.
alcohol_warning: While no direct interaction exists, alcohol should be avoided as it can worsen side effects like dizziness and stomach upset, and can dehydrate the body during infection recovery.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not take a double dose to make up for the missed one.

mechanism_of_action: It acts by promoting cervical ripening (softening and dilation) through the breakdown of collagen and stimulation of uterine smooth muscle contractions.
uses: Cervical ripening in pregnant women at or near term
Induction of labor when there is a medical or obstetrical indication
dosage_common: 0.5 mg administered endocervically; a repeat dose may be given after 6 to 12 hours if cervical ripening is not achieved, with a maximum of 1.5 mg within a 24-hour period.
overdose_effects: Can cause uterine hypercontractility and uterine hypertonus, leading to fetal distress or uterine rupture. Management involves immediate removal of residual gel and possible administration of tocolytic drugs.
contraindications: History of Cesarean section or major uterine surgery
Grand multiparity (6 or more previous term pregnancies)
drug_interactions: Oxytocin (increases risk of uterine rupture; sequential use requires careful monitoring)
pregnancy_safety: Category C/X. Indicated specifically for use in term pregnancy for labor induction; contraindicated in earlier stages unless for therapeutic abortion.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with caution in patients with hepatic or renal impairment as the drug is metabolized in these organs.
how_it_works_in_body: Dinoprostone stimulates the enzyme collagenase in the cervix, which breaks down the collagen network. This changes the physical properties of the cervix from firm to soft. Simultaneously, it increases the level of intracellular calcium in myometrial cells, triggering uterine contractions necessary for labor.
quick_summary: Cerviprime Gel is a prostaglandin medication used in hospital settings to soften the cervix and induce labor in pregnant women at term.
who_should_take: Pregnant women at term who require labor induction and have an unfavorable (unripe) cervix.
who_should_not_take: Women with prior C-sections, those with active pelvic inflammatory disease, or patients where vaginal delivery is medically unsafe.
alcohol_warning: Not applicable as it is administered during labor in a clinical setting.
missed_dose: Not applicable; this is a procedure-based medication administered by healthcare professionals.

mechanism_of_action: Cetirizine works by selectively inhibiting peripheral H1 receptors, thereby blocking the effects of histamine in the body which is responsible for allergic reactions.
dosage_common: Usually 5 mg to 10 mg once daily depending on the severity of symptoms and patient response.
side_effects_serious: Swelling of the face or throat
overdose_effects: Symptoms of overdose may include extreme somnolence, confusion, restlessness, and in children, initial agitation followed by drowsiness.
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (Creatinine Clearance less than 10 ml/min)
pregnancy_safety: Category B: Generally considered safe, but should only be used if clearly needed and prescribed by a physician.
kidney_liver_warning: Dose adjustment is necessary for patients with moderate to severe renal impairment. Caution is advised in patients with hepatic impairment.
how_it_works_in_body: After oral administration, it is rapidly absorbed. It competes with histamine for H1-receptor sites on effector cells in the gastrointestinal tract, blood vessels, and respiratory tract, preventing the histamine-mediated responses like itching, swelling, and mucus secretion.
quick_summary: CETIRIZ (Cetirizine) is a widely used antihistamine that provides relief from allergy symptoms such as sneezing, itching, watery eyes, and runny nose with a lower incidence of sedation compared to first-generation antihistamines.
who_should_take: Individuals suffering from seasonal or perennial allergic rhinitis or chronic skin allergies like hives.
who_should_not_take: Patients with end-stage renal disease, those allergic to piperazine derivatives, and infants under 6 months of age without specialist advice.
food_interactions: Can be taken with or without food
Grapefruit juice may slightly delay absorption
alcohol_warning: Consumption of alcohol while taking this medication can increase the risk of drowsiness and impaired mental alertness.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double the dose.

drug_class: Combination of Antihistamine, Analgesic/Antipyretic, and Nasal Decongestant
mechanism_of_action: Cetirizine is an H1-receptor antagonist that blocks histamine. Paracetamol inhibits prostaglandin synthesis in the central nervous system to reduce pain and fever. Phenylephrine is an alpha-1 adrenergic agonist that causes vasoconstriction in the nasal mucosa to reduce congestion.
dosage_common: Usually one tablet twice daily or as directed by a physician. Not to exceed 4 grams of Paracetamol in 24 hours.
overdose_effects: Overdose can lead to severe liver damage due to Paracetamol, extreme restlessness or high blood pressure due to Phenylephrine, and severe sedation due to Cetirizine.
pregnancy_safety: Category C: Use only if clearly needed and under strict medical supervision. Consult a doctor before use.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with extreme caution in patients with liver or kidney disease; dosage adjustment may be necessary to avoid toxicity.
how_it_works_in_body: The combination provides multi-symptom relief: Cetirizine blocks allergy triggers; Paracetamol acts on the brain's heat-regulating center and blocks pain signals; Phenylephrine shrinks swollen blood vessels in the nasal passages.
quick_summary: Cheston Cold is a widely used combination medicine in India for relieving symptoms of the common cold, allergies, and fever.
who_should_take: Individuals suffering from a combination of nasal congestion, sneezing, and fever or body ache associated with the cold or flu.
who_should_not_take: People with chronic liver disease, severe heart conditions, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or known allergies to antihistamines.
food_interactions: Can be taken with or without food
alcohol_warning: Avoid alcohol consumption as it significantly increases the risk of liver damage and enhances the sedative effect of the medicine.
missed_dose: Take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time for the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not take a double dose.

mechanism_of_action: It acts as a competitive antagonist of histamine H1-receptors and serotonin receptors. By blocking H1 receptors, it reduces allergic reactions; by blocking serotonin receptors in the hypothalamus, it helps stimulate the appetite center.
dosage_common: Adults: 4 mg three times a day, adjusted based on response. Children (7-14 years): 4 mg two to three times a day. Maximum adult dose is 32 mg per day.
overdose_effects: Overdose may lead to CNS depression followed by stimulation, dry mouth, fixed dilated pupils, flushing, and gastrointestinal symptoms. In severe cases, it can cause respiratory failure.
pregnancy_safety: Category B: Animal studies have not shown risk to the fetus, but there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Use only if clearly needed.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with caution in patients with hepatic impairment or renal failure; dosage adjustments may be necessary due to altered drug metabolism.

quick_summary: Ciplactin is a versatile antihistamine primarily used for treating allergies and as an appetite stimulant for those struggling with weight gain.
who_should_take: Individuals experiencing allergic reactions such as hay fever or itching, and patients requiring medical assistance with appetite stimulation.
who_should_not_take: Elderly patients with dementia, individuals with glaucoma, prostate enlargement, or those taking MAO inhibitors within the last 14 days.

mechanism_of_action: Clopidogrel is a prodrug that requires metabolism to its active form, which then irreversibly inhibits the P2Y12 subtype of ADP receptors on the platelet surface, preventing subsequent activation of the GPIIb/IIIa receptor complex and platelet aggregation.
dosage_common: 75 mg once daily, taken orally with or without food.
overdose_effects: Overdose may lead to prolonged bleeding time and subsequent bleeding complications. There is no known antidote; platelet transfusion may reverse effects if immediate action is required.
pregnancy_safety: Category B: Generally considered safe as animal studies show no fetal harm, but should be used only if clearly needed under a doctor's supervision.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with caution in patients with moderate to severe renal or hepatic impairment due to increased risk of bleeding complications.
how_it_works_in_body: After oral administration, it is rapidly absorbed and metabolized by the liver (primarily via CYP2C19). The active metabolite binds permanently to platelet receptors for the remainder of the platelet's lifespan (7-10 days), preventing them from sticking together to form clots.
onset_of_action: 2 hours for initial effect; 3 to 7 days for steady-state platelet inhibition.
quick_summary: CLOPIVAS 75 is a blood thinner (antiplatelet) used to reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes in patients with heart disease or recent vascular procedures.
who_should_take: Individuals with a history of heart attack, stroke, or those who have recently undergone heart stent procedures to prevent future thrombotic events.
who_should_not_take: Patients with active ulcers, those scheduled for surgery within 5-7 days, or those with known bleeding disorders.
food_interactions: Avoid Grapefruit juice as it may inhibit the enzyme required to activate the drug.
alcohol_warning: Limit alcohol consumption as it can increase the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding while on this medication.

drug_class: NSAID (Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug) and Analgesic combination
mechanism_of_action: Ibuprofen acts by inhibiting cyclooxygenase (COX) enzymes to reduce the synthesis of prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation; Paracetamol acts on the central nervous system to increase the pain threshold and regulate body temperature via the hypothalamus.
dosage_common: Usually one tablet every 4 to 6 hours as needed, not exceeding 3 tablets in 24 hours, preferably taken after meals.
overdose_effects: Can lead to severe liver damage (hepatotoxicity), renal failure, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, metabolic acidosis, and in extreme cases, coma.
pregnancy_safety: Category D - Not recommended, especially in the third trimester as it may cause premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with extreme caution; dose reduction may be necessary. Prolonged use increases the risk of analgesic nephropathy and hepatotoxicity.
how_it_works_in_body: The medicine combines the peripheral anti-inflammatory action of Ibuprofen with the central analgesic and antipyretic action of Paracetamol, providing synergistic relief for both pain and fever.
quick_summary: Combiflam is a widely used combination medicine for treating mild to moderate pain and reducing fever, belonging to the NSAID class.
who_should_take: Adults and adolescents over 12 years of age suffering from acute pain, inflammatory conditions, or high fever.
who_should_not_take: Individuals with a history of stomach ulcers, those allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs, and patients with severe organ failure.
food_interactions: Should be taken with food or milk to minimize gastric irritation.
alcohol_warning: Avoid alcohol as it significantly increases the risk of stomach bleeding and liver toxicity.
missed_dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double the dose.

drug_class: Angiotensin II Receptor Blocker (ARB) and Thiazide-like Diuretic Combination
mechanism_of_action: Telmisartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) that prevents vasoconstriction by blocking AT1 receptors. Chlorthalidone is a long-acting diuretic that inhibits sodium and chloride reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule, leading to increased excretion of water and salt.
uses: Reduction of risk of cardiovascular events in patients with hypertension
dosage_common: Usually one tablet once daily, preferably in the morning to avoid nocturnal urination, or as prescribed by a physician.
overdose_effects: Signs include severe hypotension, tachycardia or bradycardia, dizziness, electrolyte depletion, and dehydration.
pregnancy_safety: Category D. High risk. Use during the second and third trimesters can cause injury and death to the developing fetus. Must be discontinued immediately upon pregnancy detection.
kidney_liver_warning: Use with extreme caution in patients with moderate to severe renal or hepatic diseases. Periodic monitoring of serum electrolytes and creatinine is mandatory.
how_it_works_in_body: The combination exerts a synergistic effect. Telmisartan relaxes the blood vessels by blocking a hormone that causes them to narrow, while Chlorthalidone reduces the volume of fluid circulating in the blood vessels by increasing urine output. Together, they lower blood pressure more effectively than either drug alone.
quick_summary: Cresar CT is a combination medication used to treat hypertension when a single drug is not sufficient, helping to prevent heart attacks, strokes, and kidney failure.
who_should_take: Adult patients with primary hypertension whose blood pressure is not adequately controlled on monotherapy.
who_should_not_take: Pregnant women, patients with severe liver or kidney failure, and those with a known allergy to sulfonamide-derived drugs.
food_interactions: Can be taken with or without food

alcohol_warning: Alcohol consumption should be avoided as it can enhance the blood pressure lowering effect, potentially causing fainting or severe dizziness.
